title: Learning the ropes from the kitchen table
text: {{1}} the past, a new employee learned the unwritten rules {{2}} standing near the coffee machine: who to ask, what not to touch, {{3}} decisions really got made. Remote work {{4}} stripped most of that away, and companies that moved online learned {{5}} the hard way when early remote hires drifted and quietly resigned. Deliberate design had {{6}} replace accidental osmosis. Successful remote employers now script the first weeks, pair each newcomer with a colleague {{7}} explicit job is to welcome the small questions, and record short videos of how things actually work. It turns out that the informal curriculum mattered {{8}} than the official one, and that culture is not what is written on the walls but what is repeated in conversations.
